chunks: The Shaykh Abu Ja'far Muhammad b. Ali b. al-Husayn b. Musa b. Babawayh al-Qummi (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us [...] from Abu Abdullah [Imam al-Sadiq] (as).

He said: The neighbors of Umm Ayman came to the Messenger of God (s) and said: O Messenger of God, Umm Ayman did not sleep last night from weeping; she did not cease weeping until morning. He said: The Messenger of God (s) sent for Umm Ayman and she came. He said to her: O Umm Ayman, may God not cause your eyes to weep. Your neighbors came to me and informed me that you did not cease weeping all night. May God not cause your eyes to weep. What made you weep? She said: O Messenger of God, I saw a great and terrible dream, so I did not cease weeping all night. The Messenger of God (s) said to her: Describe it to the Messenger of God, for God and His Messenger know best. She said: It overwhelms me to speak of it. He said to her: The dream is not as you think, so describe it to the Messenger of God. She said: I saw this night as though some of your limbs were lying in my house.
The Messenger of God (s) said to her: May your eyes sleep, O Umm Ayman. Fatima will give birth to al-Husayn, and you will raise him and care for him, and he will be part of my limbs in your house.

When Fatima gave birth to al-Husayn (as), on the seventh day, the Messenger of God (s) ordered that his head be shaved, and charity be given equal to the weight of his hair in silver, and the aqiqa be performed for him. Then Umm Ayman prepared him and wrapped him in the cloak of the Messenger of God (s). Then she brought him to the Messenger of God (s), and he (s) said: Welcome to the carrier and the one being carried. O Umm Ayman, this is the interpretation of your dream.

key_terms.أُمِّ أَيْمَنَ: Umm Ayman - Baraka, the Prophet's freed slave and close companion who helped raise al-Husayn
key_terms.رُؤْيَا: Dream/vision - prophetic dreams interpreted by the Prophet
key_terms.عَقَّ: Aqiqa - the ritual sacrifice performed on the seventh day after a child's birth
key_terms.مَرْحَبًا بِالْحَامِلِ وَالْمَحْمُولِ: Welcome to the carrier and the carried - the Prophet's greeting to Umm Ayman carrying al-Husayn

ai.seo_question: What dream did Umm Ayman have about the birth of Imam al-Husayn?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq narrates the story of Umm Ayman, the freed slave and close companion of the Prophet, who was distressed by a dream in which she saw some of the Prophet's limbs in her house. The Prophet interpreted the dream as a prophecy that Fatima would give birth to al-Husayn, whom Umm Ayman would help raise. After al-Husayn's birth, the Prophet performed the seventh-day rituals (head-shaving, silver charity, aqiqa) and joyfully received the infant with his famous words welcoming 'the carrier and the carried.'
